production.note: US model years 2021-2026. Start: Cars.com lists a 2021 'Plaid AWD' trim (database). End year is provisional: Drive Tesla Canada (driveteslacanada-s-x-end-2026, Darryn John, 28 Jan 2026): "the company will discontinue the Model S and Model X in the second quarter of 2026" (announced by Elon Musk on the Q4 2025 earnings call); Cars.com lists a 2026 'Plaid AWD' trim (carscom-model-s-2026). Basenor (basenor-plaid-relisted-2026) reports Tesla relisted the 'Plaid Tri Motor All-Wheel Drive trim' in March 2026 while 'winding down Model S and Model X production at the Fremont factory in Q2 2026'.

configuration.note: Three motors: Tesla's US configurator trim is the 'Plaid Tri Motor All-Wheel Drive' (basenor-plaid-relisted-2026). Cars.com: '1020.0-hp, -liter, Electric Motor' (2022 page, carscom-model-s-plaid-2022).

powerHp.note: PROVISIONAL: spec database and an unsigned article. Cars.com 2021 Plaid AWD quote: "SAE Net Horsepower @ RPM: 1020" (the 2022 page is the same, carscom-model-s-plaid-2022). InsideEVs (insideevs-plaid-vs-raven, no author): "system output: 1,020 hp (about 760 kW)". Not A Tesla App (notateslaapp-plaid-specs, Kevin Armstrong, 12 Jan 2023): "Maximum Horsepower: 1,020 hp". Tesla's own 1,020 hp figure is on tesla.com, which could not be read.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL: spec database and an unsigned article. Cars.com 2021 Plaid AWD quote: "Base Curb Weight: 4,766 lbs" (2022 page the same, carscom-model-s-plaid-2022). InsideEVs (insideevs-plaid-vs-raven, no author): "Weight 4,766 lbs (2,162 kg)". Not A Tesla App (notateslaapp-plaid-specs, 2023 article) prints 4,816 lb, 1.0% higher, in an article about MotorTrend's test, so probably a tested scale weight; see discrepancies.

discrepancies.reason: 4,766 lb is given for the 2021-2022 Plaid by Cars.com and InsideEVs; 4,816 lb comes from a January 2023 article about MotorTrend's test, so it is probably a tested scale weight. The two are 1.0% apart, within the provisional-record tolerance.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 4,766 lb, given by two sources for the 2021 reference year.

provisionalNote: Power and weight rest on Cars.com (database) and InsideEVs (unsigned article), which agree on 1,020 hp and 4,766 lb; Tesla's own figures (tesla.com, unreadable here) or a major magazine's specification panel would replace them. The last model year (2026) rests on Drive Tesla Canada's report of Tesla's Q4 2025 earnings call and on Cars.com; a Tesla statement that production has ended would replace it.
